home.intro: Online party games about academic life, played in the browser. Everyone joins the same room from their own phone or laptop: pick a nickname and you're in, with no sign-up.

keywords.name: Double Blind
keywords.summary: Two research groups race to find their keywords from short clues. Reveal Reviewer 2, and your paper is rejected.

impostor.name: Spot the Impostor
impostor.summary: Everyone gets the same term except one, who gets a close cousin.

titles.name: Real or Fake
titles.summary: Tell real paper titles from invented ones.

abstracts.name: Bluff the Abstract
abstracts.summary: Write a convincing abstract for a paper nobody has read.

letter.title: Decision letter

oral.1: Dear authors of the {group}, we are delighted to inform you that your submission has been accepted to R2Conf as an oral presentation. The reviewers were struck by how far ahead you finished: the other group still had {left} keywords to find. Please prepare a twelve-minute talk, and resist the urge to fit forty slides into it.
oral.2: Dear {group}, congratulations! Out of a record number of submissions, yours is one of the very few selected for an oral at R2Conf. You found every keyword while your competitors still had {left} left on the table. The plenary hall is yours.
oral.3: Dear {group}, the program committee is pleased to accept your paper as an oral presentation. Reviewer 2 looked hard for a weakness and found none. Your rivals are still looking for {left} keywords of their own.

spotlight.1: Dear {group}, we are pleased to inform you that your paper has been accepted to R2Conf as a spotlight. It was close: the other group had only {left} keywords left to find. You will have five minutes on stage; please use them wisely.
spotlight.2: Dear {group}, congratulations on your acceptance with a spotlight presentation. The reviewers praised your clear clues and steady guessing, and noted that your rivals were just {left} keywords behind.
spotlight.3: Dear {group}, your submission has been accepted as a spotlight paper. The area chair writes: “Solid work, finished with {left} keywords to spare on the other side. We expect the camera-ready version by Friday.”

poster.1: Dear {group}, we are happy to let you know that your paper has been accepted to R2Conf as a poster. You won by a single keyword, which the reviewers called “a thrilling finish”. Please bring a poster tube and a strong voice.
poster.2: Dear {group}, after a long discussion, your paper has been accepted as a poster. The other group was one keyword away from taking your slot. Posters are A0 and portrait; the coffee is at the back.
poster.3: Dear {group}, congratulations: your paper squeezed in as a poster. One more keyword on the other side, and this letter would read very differently.

deskReject.1: Dear {group}, we regret to inform you that your submission has been desk rejected without review. Your group revealed Reviewer 2, who needed no further evidence. The {other} goes on to the conference without you.
deskReject.2: Dear {group}, your paper has been desk rejected. Reviewer 2 read the first line, wrote “major flaws throughout” and left. We wish you better luck in the next cycle.
deskReject.3: Dear {group}, thank you for your submission. Unfortunately, it was assigned to Reviewer 2, and that was the end of it: desk reject. The {other} sends its regards.

reject.1: Dear {group}, we regret to inform you that your paper was not accepted to R2Conf. The {other} found all of its keywords first, and there was room for only one of you. We received many strong submissions this year.
reject.2: Dear {group}, thank you for submitting to R2Conf. After careful consideration, the committee has decided to reject your paper. The {other} simply got there first. The reviews, all three words of them, are attached.
reject.3: Dear {group}, unfortunately your submission has been rejected. It was not a bad paper; the {other} just finished its paper sooner. We hope to see a revised version in the next game.

withdrawn.1: The chair withdrew this game before the end. The submission is closed: nobody is accepted, and nobody is rejected.
withdrawn.2: This submission has been withdrawn by the chair. No decision will be made, and no reviewer was harmed.
withdrawn.3: The chair pulled this paper before the decision. Both groups keep their keywords, and their dignity, for the next game.

rules.title: How to play
rules.goal: Two research groups, red and blue, each have keywords hidden among the 25 cards on the board. The group that finds all of its keywords first wins.
rules.roles: Each group has one PI and as many students as it likes. The PIs see which cards belong to whom; the students see only the words.

turn.free: The PI gives a clue and a number: how many cards the clue points to, from 1 to the cards the group has left. The students then reveal cards one at a time, and go on for as long as they find their group's cards. Once they have revealed a card, they may end the turn.
turn.standard: The PI gives a clue and a number: how many cards the clue points to. The students then reveal cards one at a time, up to that number plus one. With 0 or ∞ there is no limit. Once they have revealed a card, they may end the turn.

rules.reveal: One of your group's cards: go on. An irrelevant paper or a card of the other group: your turn ends, and the other group's card counts for them. Reviewer 2: your paper is rejected, and your group loses at once.

clue.zh: A clue is one word, with at most one Chinese character. | A clue is one word, with at most {count} Chinese characters.
clue.en: A clue is one word. | A clue has at most {count} words.

rules.clueCommon: It can't be a word on the board, a part of one, or the card's term in the other language. The PI says nothing else and makes no gestures.

clueRule.strict: This room's clue check is strict: a clue can't be another form of a word on the board that the word lists give, or have a Chinese character in common with one. Other forms, which the check can only guess at, bring a warning, and the PI decides.
clueRule.loose: This room's clue check is loose: other forms of a word on the board, and Chinese characters in common with one, only bring a warning, and the PI decides.

rules.time: The settings above say how much time each phase has, and the bar under the turn shows what is left.
rules.timeClue: A PI who gives no clue in time loses the turn to the other group.
rules.timeGuess: Students whose time runs out end their turn, even if they have revealed nothing.
rules.noTime: This room has no time limits.
rules.end: A group wins as soon as all its cards are revealed, even when the other group revealed the last one.
